title: Rafael and the Parish
premise: When the coffin of Rafael Ostrander, founder of the river town of Parish, is exhumed for a land dispute, Sable Kavanagh discovers it empty—and realizes the 'dead witness' in a fifteen-year-old arson case, whose testimony she once filed away, may never have died at all. As she follows a trail of falsified death certificates and buried ledgers, Sable learns that Parish's founding families built their fortune on a fire they set themselves, and that the man everyone mourns has been living in plain sight. The missing witness is Rafael himself, hiding as the parish groundskeeper, and he'll testify only if Sable can prove who ordered the fire before the statute's last loophole closes. In the end, Sable chooses justice outside the law: she exposes the truth to the town rather than the court, letting Parish bury its founder twice—once in the ground, once in memory.
about_author: Yara Montrose is a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloging the paper trails of fading mill towns before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets communities keep in filing cabinets and in silence.

chapters.title: The Weight of Good Earth
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Sable Kavanagh. At the exhumation ordered by the Ostrander estate's land dispute, the coffin of town founder Rafael Ostrander is opened before the gathered town—and it is empty. Sable, whose photographic memory catalogs every face in the crowd, notices the groundskeeper flinch. Emotional beat: the orderly world of filed secrets cracks open.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Alphabet
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She returns to the insurance archive where she works and pulls the file she's avoided: the 2009 parish hall fire, ruled accidental, one witness—Marisol Vega—declared dead before testifying. Sable remembers, word for word, the deposition Marisol never gave. Emotional beat: guilt surfaces; Sable realizes she helped close a case she never believed.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper's Hands
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. She stakes out the parish cemetery and observes the groundskeeper—calloused hands, an Ostrander jaw, a wedding band worn on a chain. When he catches her watching, he says only, 'Some men are already buried. Let them rest.' Emotional beat: dread mixed with the thrill of a puzzle finally worth solving.

chapters.title: Widow of the Founder
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Cordelia Ostrander, the founder's widow, who orchestrated the exhumation for reasons she tells no one: she received a letter in her dead husband's handwriting three weeks ago. She must learn if the man she mourned betrayed her twice. Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury.

chapters.title: Marisol Vega, Deceased
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable tracks Marisol Vega's death certificate and finds the signing physician died himself a year later—and his signature on the certificate doesn't match his known hand. Someone manufactured a death. Emotional beat: the quiet horror of paperwork as a murder weapon.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Marisol's voice, reconstructed from Sable's memory. The night of the fire: Marisol saw three cars leave the parish hall before it burned, one of them Rafael Ostrander's. She fled town that morning; by evening she was legally dead. Emotional beat: terror of a witness with no country.

chapters.title: The Founding Families
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable maps the fire's insurance payout—$2.4 million split among four founding families, including the Ostranders—and finds the parish hall sat on land now worth thirty times more. The fire wasn't tragedy; it was zoning. Emotional beat: cynicism hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: A Visit at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Someone ransacks the archive overnight; the Vega file is gone, but Sable has already memorized it. Sheriff Dale Pruitt, whose father signed the original report, warns her off with a smile that doesn't reach his eyes. Emotional beat: the town closing ranks around her.

chapters.title: The Letter in the Mailbox
chapters.summary: Cordelia's POV. Cordelia confronts the groundskeeper at the cemetery gate; he neither confirms nor denies, but he returns her wedding photograph, lost for fifteen years. She understands: her husband is alive and has been watching her grieve. Emotional beat: betrayal sharper than mourning.

chapters.title: Buried Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following the groundskeeper's night rounds, Sable finds a cache beneath the cemetery chapel: Rafael's own ledgers documenting the arson scheme, kept as insurance against his partners. The last page names the man who gave the order—not Rafael. Emotional beat: the founder was both architect and prisoner.

chapters.title: The Man Who Gave the Order
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The name is Ambrose Pruitt—the current sheriff's father, the town's other founding patriarch, dead two years and untouchable. But the statute's final loophole requires a living conspirator, and Rafael's ledgers show one: the payout was laundered through a trust that still operates. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline.

chapters.title: Grounds for Conversation
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable finally corners Rafael among the headstones. He confesses everything except the order itself: he set the fire on instruction, then faked his death when the partners decided Marisol's death certificate needed a matching founder's. Emotional beat: pity for a man who chose a coffin over a conscience.

chapters.title: He Will Not Testify
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, first time in his own voice. Rafael refuses to testify: the trust's beneficiary is Cordelia's brother, and exposure will destroy her. He has spent fifteen years protecting her from a truth that would be worse than grief. Emotional beat: love as an argument for silence.

chapters.title: The Sheriff's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dale Pruitt's POV. Dale knows Sable is close; his father's ledgers are half of the story, and the trust pays his salary through a shell. He begins building a case against Sable instead—evidence tampering, a break-in she didn't commit. Emotional beat: a decent man choosing the rot he inherited.

chapters.title: Arrested Memory
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable is detained on fabricated charges; in the interrogation room she recites the fire file from memory, word for word, daring Dale to explain how she could know what was never in any report. He goes pale. Emotional beat: her memory, once a cage, becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Choice
chapters.summary: Cordelia's POV. Cordelia reads the ledgers Rafael left for her and learns her brother ordered the fire and her husband's erasure. She must decide which family to bury. She chooses the living: she calls Sable and offers the trust documents. Emotional beat: grief finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: The Last Filing Day
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. With Cordelia's documents and Rafael's ledgers, Sable has the whole architecture of the conspiracy—but Dale moves to destroy the archive with a court-ordered 'evidence seizure' at dawn. Sable has one night to get the truth somewhere it can't be seized. Emotional beat: the clock running loud.

chapters.title: Testimony at the Graveyard
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Before dawn, Sable summons the town to the cemetery—not to court, but to the founder's empty grave—and Rafael rises from among the headstones to tell them everything: the fire, the payout, the trust, the name. Emotional beat: a town forced to witness itself.

chapters.title: What the Town Decided
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The legal system stalls—Dale destroys the seized papers, the trust's lawyers circle—but the town has already ruled. Parish's businesses cut the trust's ties, Cordelia's brother flees, and Dale resigns under the weight of four hundred watching neighbors. Emotional beat: justice as a verdict the town hands down itself.

chapters.title: The Second Funeral
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The town buries the empty coffin again, this time with full knowledge, and the ceremony is strangely honest. Cordelia stands apart from the Ostrander plot; Marisol Vega's name is read aloud among the honored dead, though she is alive and watching from the back. Emotional beat: mourning as an act of truth.

chapters.title: Marisol Comes Home
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol returns to Parish for the first time in fifteen years and finds her own name on a restored memorial plaque. Sable gives her back the deposition she never got to give—not to a court, but to the town record, where it will outlive everyone who feared it. Emotional beat: a witness finally heard.

chapters.title: Alphabet of the Living
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reorganizes the archive, moving the fire file from 'Closed' to 'Ongoing' and starting a new drawer labeled with the names of the living who deserve watching—including, she admits with a smile, her own. Some secrets should stay filed; others should be set loose. Emotional beat: belonging, earned through truth rather than silence.
